The `brgybnd` toolchain is configured via environment variables (read by `config.py` with
`python-dotenv`). The LLM-related variables are only required for the optional
[Pipeline A](pipeline-rdf.qmd) agent batch-extraction step.

## Variables

| Variable           | Default                                          | Purpose |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------|---------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY`   | *(none — required for LLM agent pipeline)*       | API key for the OpenAI-compatible LLM client |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL`  | `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/` (GLM API)        | Base URL of the OpenAI-compatible endpoint |
| `OPENAI_MODEL`     | `glm-4.7`                                        | Model name for structured-output extraction |
| `PSGC_DATA_DIR`    | `~/commons/barangay`                             | Directory holding the PSGC snapshot source files |

## .env example

A `.env` in the repository root (loaded by `config.py` via `python-dotenv`) only needs the data
directory in practice; the three `OPENAI_*` vars are for the optional
[Pipeline A](pipeline-rdf.qmd) LLM step and can be omitted for offline runs:

```bash
# required to point at the PSGC snapshot source tree
PSGC_DATA_DIR=~/commons/barangay

# optional — only for the LLM batch-extraction step of Pipeline A
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/
OPENAI_MODEL=glm-4.7
```

`PSGC_DATA_DIR` is the **root** of the snapshot tree. `ingest/scanner.py` expects each snapshot as a
per-quarter subdirectory named `YYYY-MM-DD/` (e.g. `2023-10-24/`) containing the PSA Excel datafile,
the changes sheet(s), and the PDF press release — it classifies the files inside by filename regex.
Pointing `PSGC_DATA_DIR` anywhere else just relocates that tree.

The GLM defaults (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_MODEL`) target the Z.ai GLM endpoint; set them to any
OpenAI-compatible base URL and structured-output model of your choice.
